mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Compact Robotic Palletizer Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The TRFCompact Dual has a reference list price of US$ 180,000, EX Works Lenexa, Kansas, installation not included. Installation, line integration, gripper and conveyor interface are quoted with your application, because line speed, case weight, pallet pattern and layout change the scope. Use the payback calculator on this page to estimate what manual palletizing costs you today.

mainEntity.name: How Much Floor Space Does a Compact Palletizing Cell Require?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the robot reach, the number of pallet positions, the infeed layout and the access your operators and forklifts need. TRFCompact is designed for brownfield environments and lines where production space has high value, so the cell is laid out on your plant drawing during the application review. TRF confirms the footprint for your pallet pattern and pallet height before the quote.

mainEntity.name: Can a Compact Palletizer Be Installed in a Brownfield Plant With Limited Space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Brownfield plants where floor space is a major limitation are one of the core applications of TRFCompact. The platform combines an industrial robot with a compact, standardized cell, so it can fit next to an existing line without the footprint of a traditional large robotic cell. TRF validates layout, reach and pallet flow against your drawing and your existing conveyors.

mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for My Product?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the case weight plus the end-of-arm tool, and the combined weight when it picks more than one case at a time. TRFCompact handles cases up to about 44 lb, TRFCobot up to about 22 lb and TRFSpeed up to about 66 lb. These are typical ranges: TRF validates the final payload with your product, gripper, pallet pattern and reach.

mainEntity.name: How Does a Robotic Palletizer Handle SKU or Pallet Pattern Changeovers?

acceptedAnswer.text: A changeover usually means selecting a stored recipe that holds the case dimensions, pick logic and pallet pattern for the new SKU. When the new case fits the same end-of-arm tool, the change happens mostly in software. TRFCompact keeps multiple SKU recipes and pallet patterns on an industrial platform, so a high-mix line changes products without a new project.

mainEntity.name: Can a Palletizer Be Integrated With My Existing Conveyor and Wrapping Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, when the interfaces are defined in the application study: case infeed rate and orientation, spacing, signals between machines and how full pallets travel to the stretch wrapper. TRF engineers these interfaces as part of the project and can supply TRFIntraflow conveyors where the line needs accumulation, routing or elevation. See end-of-line integration for the full-line approach.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical Payback Period for a Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The estimate follows the method of the A3 (Association for Advancing Automation) robot ROI calculator: the system cost, including 20 years of maintenance at 5% per year, divided by the annual net savings, which is the labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses. The calculator on this page applies this method to your location, your shifts and the people who palletize by hand today, and returns an initial estimate that a TRF Sales Engineer completes with the costs of your project.

mainEntity.name: What Maintenance Does a Robotic Palletizer Require to Avoid Downtime?

acceptedAnswer.text: A robotic palletizer needs periodic inspection of the gripper, sensors and the robot itself, following the manufacturer's schedule, plus replacement of wear parts before they fail. For TRF-supplied equipment, Parts and Service covers technical support, spare parts kept in the United States and the TRFCare preventive maintenance program.

mainEntity.name: Who Makes Robotic Case Palletizers With Local Support in the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRF designs, builds, installs and supports robotic case palletizers, including TRFCompact, for manufacturers across the United States. The same partner can supply the case packers and conveyors around the palletizer, so the end of line is engineered as one project, with one point of contact from the application review to startup and technical support.
